what: the 704/78 memorisation diagnostic on DANN x nb3 against its lambda=0 control, folds 1-4, 16 checkpoints per fold per arm (PROJECTv7 7.54)
status: retrospective, unregistered: decided 2026-10-24 after all results were known; in no pre-registration
brief: brief_dann_memorisation_diagnostic.md (author's Downloads; not in the repo)
author_decisions_2026_10_24: Option A: the main analysis uses deterministic aug='none' views for both arms on all folds
the known-null replays 7.29's exact random sequence; folds 2-4 must match at four decimals; fold 1 is excluded from the value check; weight equality is checked on all four folds
the model is built from each checkpoint's own config via TrainConfig/Trainer, as 7.29's drivers do (not the runner's build_arm)
the trained-on probe is checked against BNM's recorded probe (DANN's and lambda=0's run configs record only the holdout); the holdout against both arms' run configs
local RTX 4050, fp32 (amp=False); device, GPU name and torch version recorded

inputs.note: holdout indices: dann_d_holdout_indices in each DANN and lambda=0 run_config.json; trained-on probe: trainedon_probe.probe in each BNM run_config.json. Tars are re-hashed by the driver before extraction.

views.main: aug='none': one deterministic view per image (stretch + resize), materialised once per fold and reused for every checkpoint of both arms
views.why: it adds no augmentation noise, it is exactly reproducible, and both arms see identical images, so the DANN - lambda=0 contrast is unaffected
views.known_null: aug='weak': 7.29's one fixed weak-augmented view per image, recreated by replaying 7.29's driver's exact call sequence

statistic.definition: unchanged from 7.20: for each checkpoint, normalised nuclear norm ||A||*, mean prediction entropy and predicted-positive fraction on the size-matched 78-image trained-on probe and on the 78-image holdout, through bnm_round6.probe_stats; gap = trained-on - holdout (bnm_round6.holdout_gap)
statistic.slices: holdout = dann_round5.build_target_holdout(frac=0.10, seed=42+fold); probe = bnm_round6.build_trainedon_probe(seed=42+fold); both asserted equal to the recorded indices on every fold before anything is computed
statistic.model: TrainConfig/Trainer from the checkpoint's own cfg, init_head_from=None, amp=False, grad_checkpointing=False; Trainer.load(load_training_state=False); head in eval mode; inference only
statistic.per_checkpoint_checks: schedule.global_step == step; schedule.fold and schedule.arm match the run; cfg fold, n_blocks, lr, weight_decay, batch_size, head_type, lr_decay equal the run_config; cfg.seed == 42 + fold

primary.what: the gap at step 4000 (the pre-registered read-off of both arms)
primary.contrast: DANN - lambda=0, paired t on the four per-fold differences, df = 3, 95% (analyze_lambda0_r6.paired_t)

secondary.what: the within-fold mean of the gap over the 16 checkpoints

descriptive_only.what: the any-checkpoint maximum, per arm and per fold
descriptive_only.reason: a maximum over noisy reads has a positive null (7.28): the maximum of 16 noisy reads is positive whether or not any gap exists

readings.own_arm: each arm's own fold-mean gap at step 4000 and as the within-fold mean, with its paired-t interval against zero, labelled descriptive
readings.numbering_note: 7.27 numbers the readings (1) read-off, (2) any-checkpoint maximum, (3) within-fold mean; here primary = 7.27 (1), secondary = 7.27 (3), descriptive = 7.27 (2)
readings.number_format: [Δ] [CI] is filled as '+0.0000 [−0.0000, +0.0000]', four decimals, Unicode minus

interpretation_VERBATIM.excludes_zero_positive: Having a target objective is accompanied by a measurable gap between trained-on and held-out target images: DANN − λ=0 = [Δ] [CI] at the read-off step.
interpretation_VERBATIM.excludes_zero_negative: DANN's trained-on vs held-out gap is smaller than its control's: [Δ] [CI].
interpretation_VERBATIM.includes_zero: Whether part of the adaptation gain comes from fitting these particular target images remains undetermined: DANN − λ=0 = [Δ] [CI] at the read-off step.
interpretation_VERBATIM.includes_zero_secondary_rule: The secondary reading is then reported only together with the statement that it is the secondary.
interpretation_VERBATIM.in_every_case: In every case: no multiplicity correction, and the intervals are probably too narrow because the folds' target pools overlap (paper §5.3).

known_null.what: lambda=0 at step 4000 must reproduce 7.29 (from resume/latest.pt): +0.2128 / -0.1362 / +0.0624 / -0.0569 on folds 1-4
known_null.procedure: replay 7.29's driver's call sequence exactly: folds 1..4 in order; per fold the aug='weak' dataset, the slices, both materialisations, then Trainer(cfg from resume/latest.pt) (which seeds torch with 42 + fold, so it fixes the views of fold + 1), weights loaded from the tar's step_4000.pt; and per fold check step_4000.pt against resume/latest.pt by tensor equality (head, standardizer, trainable encoder blocks)
known_null.tolerance: equal at four decimals (the printed token, and the stored json value rounded) on folds 2, 3 and 4
known_null.fold1_exclusion: 7.29 drew its fold-1 views before anything seeded torch, and torch's default seed on this install is time-based (two fresh processes draw different numbers), so those views cannot be recreated. Fold 1's replay value is computed and reported, not checked. Its weight equality IS checked.

rules.weights identical, a checked gap differs: STOP and report (the pipeline differs from 7.29's)
rules.weights not identical on any fold: report the difference and the gaps; STOP for the author

disclosures.lambda0_views_differ: The main tables' λ=0 step-4000 gaps differ from 7.29's because the views differ (no augmentation here vs one weak-augmented view in 7.29). Both sets are reported side by side. These values are not directly comparable with BNM's logged gaps (7.28), which used weak-augmented views.
disclosures.paired_t_import: analyze_lambda0_r6 imports the metrics module at import time; nothing in it is called, and no test logits, test labels or scorer output are read

driver_edit_rule: if the driver is edited after this plan is written, the plan is not rewritten; the edit goes into results.json as driver_edits_after_plan with the reason
